newsitem.title: CHINA: China insurer aims for $120 million profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China insurer aims for $120 million profit in 1997.

text.p: China's Pingan Insurance Co has set a profit target of 1.0 billion yuan ($120 million) in 1997, the Financial News said in an edition seen on Friday.
The company plans to make at least 800 million yuan in profits this year, the newspaper quoted company president Ma Mingzhe as saying.
He did not give comparative figures and did not say whether the figure was pre-tax.
The Shenzhen-based insurer aims to boost its premium income to 20 billion yuan in 1997, he said. It plans to generate at least 18 billion yuan in premiums this year.
Premiums from life insurance alone were expected to reach 13 billion yuan, he said.
Pingan recorded premium income of 10.5 billion yuan in 1996, boosted by the booming life insurance business, company officials have said. Premiums from life insurance topped 7 billion yuan.
Pingan has become China's second largest underwriter in terms of premium income, capturing 14 percent of the domestic insurance market overall last year, company officials have said.
The company surpassed Shanghai-based China Pacific Insurance Co last year in overall premiums. State-owned People's Insurance Company of China was the industry leader.
